subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: What permanent public retry contract should OpenClaw expose for main LLM requests: provider-level, agent/global, both, or no new config surface?
rationale: The requested fix adds public configuration and changes provider/fallback runtime behavior; repository policy treats config/default and provider-routing changes as compatibility-sensitive, and the open related PRs currently cover only partial shapes.

options.title: Settle provider-level retry first
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98110 as the config direction only after maintainers approve the API and require follow-up runtime wiring before closing this issue.

options.title: Design an agent/global retry policy
options.body: Hold the provider-level PR and specify an `agents.defaults` style policy with retry classes, backoff array, total cap, and notification semantics.

options.title: Reject new retry config for now
options.body: Keep only existing failover, cooldown, and cron retry paths, and close the feature direction once maintainers explicitly decide the extra config surface is not worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Settle provider-level retry first
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98110 as the config direction only after maintainers approve the API and require follow-up runtime wiring before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the active maintainer-labeled same-model retry/failover PR that is closest to the product direction decision, while the provider-config PR remains external and partial.
